subject: ACME DPA - incident notification timelines & evidence handover coordination
messages:
From: Sasha Mendoza <sasha.mendoza@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@vendorsec.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification timelines & subprocessor cooperation

Karthik, thanks for the quick intake call this morning. A few narrow asks from ACME Legal and VendorSec as we look to finalize the DPA redlines: 

- Notification window: ACME's counsel is pushing for a 24-hour "initial notification" for any confirmed breach affecting ACME data. Can Redwood commit to that, and if not, what is the shortest SLO you can accept?

- Evidence handover: we need a clear timeline for delivery of forensic artifacts (logs, exports, packet captures if applicable). VendorSec is asking for delivery within 72 hours once evidence collection is complete. Is that feasible?

- Subprocessor cooperation: we will likely need Redwood to coordinate with a subprocessor (a cloud egress partner). Please confirm whether Redwood will: (a) notify us of which subprocessor(s) were involved within 24 hours of confirmation and (b) provide a secure, encrypted export of ACME-scoped data on request.

We also still have the cross-border question: if exports contain EU data, can Redwood limit transfer to EU-located stores or provide evidence via an EU-located portal?

I've attached the ACME suggested redline (see attachment 1). Please loop in your legal/ops folks. We are targeting final execution before May 5 to meet our audit.

Thanks,
Sasha Mendoza
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
ACME Health

(attachment: ACME_DPA_redline_20270424.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Mendoza <sasha.mendoza@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@vendorsec.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification timelines & subprocessor cooperation

Sasha — appreciate the clarity and the redline. High level response and proposed compromise below; I copied ops/legal so they can chime in with operational constraints.

1) Initial notification window
- Redwood can commit to an "initial notification" inside 48 hours for confirmed incidents that materially affect ACME data. We define "initial notification" as: we will (a) tell you the impacted subsystem, (b) provide a high-level summary of the impact, and (c) list immediate mitigation steps we've taken.
- For highly time-sensitive customers we can offer a 24-hour SLA via a dedicated contract or expedited incident SLA addendum (we can scope cost/operational impact if ACME prefers this).

2) Evidence handover
- We can deliver a forensics package (logs, relevant exports, and a manifest) within 72 hours of evidence-gathering completion for standard cases. In complex cross-system incidents this may take longer; we will provide cadence updates every 24 hours until delivery.

3) Subprocessor notification & exports
- We will provide a current subprocessor roster within 24 hours of request (CSV attached).
- We can produce an encrypted export of ACME-scoped data. For EU data, we can stage the export in an EU region (subject to customer account configuration and available deployment region).

Operational notes: Forensic exports are provided over an SFTP or pre-signed secure storage link; data will be encrypted at rest in transit. We may need a minimal legal transfer step (DPA exhibit/POA) for particularly sensitive artifacts.

Next steps: I'm attaching a Redwood redline of the DPA (Redwood_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Marissa/Ben/Laura — please confirm the 48/72 cadence as acceptable or propose firm language for the DPA section.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
(attachment: Redwood_DPA_redline_v3.docx)

Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification timelines & subprocessor cooperation

Adding a couple operational clarifications from Redwood Ops/Legal: 

- "Confirmed incident" definition: we should add a short definition in the DPA: an incident confirmed by Redwood's incident response team after triage that indicates unauthorized access to customer-controlled data. This avoids chasing false positives and gives us a clean start point for the clock.

- Evidence detail & export format: for the forensics packet we deliver a manifest + JSON-formatted logs + tarball of exports. If packet captures are requested they may require longer chain-of-custody and we will notify ACME before collection.

- Preservation window & snapshot: we recommend adding a clause that preserves relevant RW system snapshots for up to 90 days unless otherwise agreed. This protects both parties during investigations.

- Subprocessor coordination: Redwood will attempt to obtain cooperation from downstream subprocessors within 24 hours of request but cannot guarantee their internal routing timelines; we will include their point-of-contact in the incident thread and escalate as needed.

If ACME is amenable, here's suggested DPA language to insert: 
"Upon confirmation of an incident materially affecting Customer Data, Redwood will provide initial notification within forty-eight (48) hours and a forensics package within seventy-two (72) hours of completion of evidence collection. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to coordinate with subprocessors and disclose involved subprocessors within twenty-four (24) hours of incident confirmation. All evidence transfer will be performed over encrypted channels and, where requested by Customer for lawful reasons, will be staged in Customer-specified regions subject to operational availability."

I'll drop this language into the redline and re-upload by EOD.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: DPA — incident notification timelines & evidence handover coordination

Marissa/Karthik — thanks for the pragmatic language. ACME is comfortable with the 48/72 framework provided the following minor edits are accepted: 

1) We need a guaranteed subprocessor disclosure within 24 hours of confirmation (not "commercially reasonable efforts"). Is Redwood able to accept that as contractual commitment?

2) For EU data, ACME requires evidence to be staged in an EU-located export repo unless otherwise authorized in writing. Please confirm that Redwood will honor region constraints for accounts with EU data residency.

3) Please add a short SLA for interrupted evidence delivery: if we do not receive the forensics package within the agreed windows, Redwood will provide daily status updates and an estimated delivery ETA until complete.

If you can accept those edits we can route the redline to procurement and sign by May 3.

Sasha Mendoza
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
ACME Health
